stops.note: a split length of wood; the same word gave English 'ski' via Norwegian
first a plank or beam for sliding heavy loads, then a brake shoe on a wheel; later, the verb 'slide sideways out of control' came from wheels locked by the brake and sliding
stops.meaning: a wooden runner or plank; later to slide uncontrollably

current_meaning: to slide sideways out of control; a sliding motion
